title: Sort Integers by The Power Value
summary: Define the power of an integer x as the count of steps required to reduce x to 1 by repeatedly applying the following: if x is even, divide it by 2; if x is odd, multiply it by 3 and add 1.
statement: Define the power of an integer x as the count of steps required to reduce x to 1 by repeatedly applying the following: if x is even, divide it by 2; if x is odd, multiply it by 3 and add 1. For instance, the power of 3 is 7. Given integers lo, hi, and k, sort all integers in the range [lo, hi] by their power values in ascending order. If two integers have the same power value, sort them by their natural order. Return the k^th integer in the sorted list.
constraints: Power is the number of Collatz steps to reach one.
Sort by power then integer value and return the one-based kth value.
hints: Recursively use one plus the power of x/2 when even or 3x+1 when odd.
Sort the inclusive range by (power,value) and choose k-1.
The recurrence follows the unique Collatz trajectory, and the tuple key implements both rankings.
editorial: The recurrence follows the unique Collatz trajectory, and the tuple key implements both rankings.
